narration: Startups often discover critical bottlenecks and retry storms only after deploying, causing catastrophic downtime. Project Venessa lets teams stress-test and harden distributed architectures before writing deployment code.
action_description: Initial view of the Project Venessa dashboard showcasing the complete architecture canvas and pre-mortem simulation controls.

narration: The canvas models your full topology, from load balancers down to caches and databases. Selecting any node opens the Inspector to reveal replica counts, concurrency limits, and latency profiles.
action_description: Hover over the service graph and click on a service node to display its replica count, concurrency limits, and latency percentiles in the Node Inspector.

narration: We pick an explicit failure scenario: Cache Kill at Peak Surge. This injects a three-times traffic surge followed by an abrupt cache termination at seven hundred seconds.
action_description: Select 03_cache_kill_at_peak from the Scenario dropdown and highlight the injected failure events in the Scenario Events panel.

narration: Hitting Run Scenario triggers the SimPy discrete-event engine. Hundreds of thousands of synthetic requests stream through system queues, evaluating queue limits and timeout cascades in milliseconds.
action_description: Click the Run Scenario button in the top navigation bar and observe the simulation execution overlay.

narration: The Verdict flags a catastrophic outage, breaching our service level objective for over one hundred seconds with a forty-four percent peak error rate and thousands of dropped transactions.
action_description: Inspect the red Verdict card and hover across the key performance indicators showing peak error rate and recovery status.

narration: The Failure Story reveals the chain reaction: cache termination backed up the database, saturated connection pools, and triggered an amplified retry storm. Clicking any step jumps directly to that moment.
action_description: Scroll down the Failure Story timeline in the right sidebar and click the cascade event where database connection pools saturated.

narration: The interactive timeline replays the incident second by second. Dragging across the error curve visualizes real-time queue saturation as services turn from healthy green to failing red.
action_description: Click the Play button on the timeline scrubber, then drag the scrub head through the incident peak to watch node statuses dynamically shift color.

narration: Venessa's AI Adversary synthesizes targeted failure vectors against single points of failure. Engineers can test database slowdowns, network partitions, or gateway timeouts with one click.
action_description: Hover through the AI Adversary vectors in the left sidebar, pointing out which scenarios break the SLO envelope versus those that survive.

narration: Under Targeted Fixes, Gemini synthesizes evidence-based remediations for the exposed failure points, recommending database read replicas and exponential backoff with jitter.
action_description: Review the Targeted Fixes card highlighting recommendations to add read replicas and configure exponential backoff on retry edges.

narration: Applying the fix patches the architecture and instantly re-simulates. Switching to Compare mode reveals the before-and-after contrast: the error curve flattens completely and the system survives.
action_description: Click Apply fix & re-simulate, then click the Compare button in the top navigation to view side-by-side error curves demonstrating complete recovery.

narration: Teams can also evolve designs using the prompt bar. Prompt in plain English or edit the YAML spec, and Gemini recompiles the topology and runs validation checks instantly.
action_description: Demonstrate the bottom prompt dock by typing an architectural enhancement instruction and previewing the action.

narration: Built with FastAPI, SimPy, Google Gemini, and React, Project Venessa transforms architectural blindspots into verified resilience, safeguarding Day-One deployments.
action_description: Return to the main Architecture view and showcase the final hardened architecture running cleanly with zero dropped requests.
